job.style: a market or shop situation that uses the idea

passage: In a local market, a shopkeeper organizes his stock of sweets. He has two types of boxes: one containing 12 pieces and another containing 18 pieces. To ensure he has equal stacks of each, he calculates the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of 12 and 18. He writes 12 as 2 squared times 3, and 18 as 2 times 3 squared. By taking the highest power of each prime factor present, he finds the LCM is 36. He also notes that the Highest Common Factor (HCF) is 6, obtained by taking the lowest power of common prime factors. He reminds his assistant that while the product of two numbers equals the product of their HCF and LCM, this rule does not apply to three different types of boxes. Later, a customer asks if the ratio of the box dimensions, which is 22 divided by 7, makes the value irrational. The shopkeeper explains that 22/7 is a rational approximation, but the true value of pi is indeed irrational. Finally, he checks a new batch of 4 raised to the power n sweets, noting that since 4 only contains the prime factor 2, it can never end in the digit 0, regardless of the value of n.

items.evidence: By taking the highest power of each prime factor present, he finds the LCM is 36.
items.q: How does the shopkeeper get 36 as the LCM of 12 and 18?
options: Multiply 2 squared by 3 squared
Multiply 2 and 3, each at lowest power
Multiply all prime factors of 12 and 18
Multiply 12 by 18 straight away
items.explain: The LCM takes the highest power of each prime: 2 squared × 3 squared = 36.

wrong.why: thinks LCM uses the smallest powers
thinks you multiply every prime factor of both numbers
thinks the LCM must be bigger, so it multiplies the two numbers

items.evidence: He also notes that the Highest Common Factor (HCF) is 6, obtained by taking the lowest power of common prime factors.
items.q: Why is the HCF of 12 and 18 equal to 6 and not 36?
options: It takes the lowest power of shared primes
It takes the highest power of shared primes
It multiplies every prime factor of both
It takes only the primes not shared
items.explain: The HCF uses the lowest power of the common primes: 2 × 3 = 6.

wrong.why: thinks HCF uses the greatest power
thinks HCF multiplies all prime factors
mixes up common and non-common factors

items.evidence: He reminds his assistant that while the product of two numbers equals the product of their HCF and LCM, this rule does not apply to three different types of boxes.
items.q: What mistake does the shopkeeper warn his assistant against?
options: Using HCF × LCM = product for three numbers
Using HCF × LCM = sum for two numbers
Using highest powers when finding the LCM
Using lowest powers when finding the HCF
items.explain: HCF × LCM equals the product only for two numbers, not for three box types.

wrong.why: thinks HCF × LCM is linked to the sum
thinks the LCM should use smaller powers
thinks the HCF should use greater powers

items.evidence: The shopkeeper explains that 22/7 is a rational approximation, but the true value of pi is indeed irrational.
items.q: What is the difference between 22/7 and the true value of pi?
options: 22/7 is rational, but pi is irrational
Both are irrational, as their decimals are long
22/7 is irrational, but pi is rational
Both are rational, since 22/7 equals pi
items.explain: 22/7 is only a rational approximation; the true value of pi is irrational.

wrong.why: thinks any long decimal is irrational
thinks the approximation is exactly pi

items.evidence: Finally, he checks a new batch of 4 raised to the power n sweets, noting that since 4 only contains the prime factor 2, it can never end in the digit 0, regardless of the value of n.
items.q: Why can 4 raised to the power n never end in the digit 0?
options: Because it has the prime 2 but never 5
Because he tested many values of n
Because a factor of 2 alone gives 0
Because 4 is not a prime number itself
items.explain: Ending in 0 needs both 2 and 5; 4 to the power n only has the prime 2.

wrong.why: thinks you must check many values of n
thinks 2 alone is enough to end in 0
gives a true fact about 4 that is not the reason
